sources.entry: dictate by Vimal Kumar - Local, offline voice-to-text for Claude Code on Linux built on faster-whisper, with a warm daemon for instant transcription, system-wide push-to-talk, a voice-enabled editor, and per-project vocabulary hints that fix technical terms ("Claude" not "cloud"). summary.one_liner: A local, offline voice-to-text tool for Linux desktops that records speech on a push-to-talk key and pastes the transcription, built on faster-whisper.
summary.what_it_does: Runs a background daemon that keeps a Whisper model loaded in memory, so transcription starts without per-request delay. A separate push-to-talk service listens system-wide via evdev for a trigger key (Right Ctrl by default), records while held, and plays a bell when transcription is ready so the user can paste with Ctrl+V. It includes a voice-enabled nvim editor (dictate-editor) for longer prompts, and a /dictate Claude Code command. Per-project and global vocabulary hint files are merged and sent with each request to improve recognition of technical terms. It can also run a headless TCP transcription server on a LAN GPU machine that laptops forward audio to, and it switches transcription languages on the fly. Mic and keyboard disconnects are detected and reported with desktop notifications.
use_cases: dictating prompts into Claude Code without typing
offline speech-to-text on a Linux desktop
private voice transcription with no cloud or API keys
offloading Whisper transcription to a GPU machine on the LAN
fixing technical term misrecognition with custom vocabulary
bilingual dictation with quick language switching
how_to_run: Install the missing system packages the installer lists, add your user to the input group, log out and back in, then run bash install.sh again
notable: Push-to-talk works system-wide in any window, including Claude Code, with no special integration
Warm daemon keeps the Whisper model in memory and a 1-second rolling pre-buffer captures speech from key press
Per-project vocabulary hints (.dictate-hints.d/) are sent per request, so no daemon restart is needed
Network mode lets a laptop without a GPU forward raw float32 audio to a GPU server over TCP
Mic health monitoring and keyboard hot-plug detection, with automatic recalibration
caveats: Linux only, requires PipeWire; README says tested on Fedora 43/44 and Ubuntu 22.04/24.04
Installer needs system packages and input group membership (sudo commands run manually), and evdev compiles from source
Jetson (aarch64) requires building ctranslate2 from source first
Default model quality depends on hardware: small on CPU, medium on NVIDIA GPU; large-v3 needs more than 4GB VRAM
